source.title: Grokking Is Conditional and Fragile: A Fully-Tractable, Multi-Seed Study at 12K Parameters

page_placements.theme: Numerical effects on spikes and individual outcomes

record.tranche_reason: Tests algorithmic grokking, weight-decay dependence, coverage thresholds, and numerical sensitivity in a different model and experimental regime; it does not reproduce the original study’s full training-trajectory analysis across training-set sizes.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the study’s own results on modular-arithmetic grokking, weight decay, numerical-environment comparisons, and mechanistic read-outs. Claims cited from other work are not recorded as results. The paper reports best held-out accuracy and grok-rates for many conditions, but those summaries alone do not reveal when grokking occurred.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes a pretrained ~12K-parameter transformer on modular arithmetic and reports its own results. These include a held-out accuracy trajectory (V1), grok-rate across training coverage and weight decay (V5), and numerical-environment perturbations. The setting and the grok-rate measure differ from the originals, but the question is the same.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that grokking here is a conditional, fragile phase transition: gated by coverage (with a threshold set mainly by the modulus), promoted then destroyed by weight decay, and flipped per seed by floating-point reduction order without changing the aggregate rate. Output periodicity is a partly definitional correlate, and the independent mechanistic result is the absence of a Fourier embedding circle. Decomposition helps by making coverage dense. Methodologically, single-seed grokking narratives mislead, so multi-seed rates under a pinned numerical environment are required.
record.recipe_differences: Fine-tunes a pretrained ≈11,856-parameter Llama-style model on text-form modular arithmetic, with multi-seed grok-rate and coverage sweeps; the original is cited as prior work, not explicitly replicated. This study also varies numerical environment, weight decay, and task decomposition.
record.method_sensitivity: Coverage, modulus/output cardinality, composition structure, weight decay, CPU thread count, execution device, grok threshold, and seed affect reported grok-rates or individual outcomes. Thread count and device changes alter which seeds grok but do not detectably shift aggregate rate.

fits_no_version.finding: Changing reduction order (1 vs 4 CPU threads) or device (CPU vs GPU) flips 49/300 and 19/100 same-seed grok outcomes, with no detectable aggregate grok-rate shift (McNemar p=0.39 and 1.0).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Individual grokking outcomes are sensitive to sub-ULP floating-point differences, while the aggregate grok-rate is not.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed coverage, grok-rate falls with the modulus (100% for M≤8, 50% at M=9, 30% at M=10 at 60% coverage). The pattern is non-monotone near threshold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The coverage threshold for grokking scales with output cardinality more than with composition structure.

fits_no_version.finding: Output-logit Fourier concentration correlates with held-out accuracy, but embedding Fourier concentration does not, and there is no Fourier embedding circle at hidden size 16.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a very narrow model, generalizing modular solutions are periodic in their output map without a clean Fourier-circle embedding.

fits_no_version.finding: At a matched 160-example budget, a specialist pipeline groks (4/10, 10/10) where direct and scratchpad monoliths groke 0/10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task decomposition aids grokking by turning sparse composite coverage into dense sub-task coverage.

record.problems: The study uses a single toy architecture and modular arithmetic with M ≤ 10. Some coverage cells use only 3–5 seeds and the authors call their thresholds provisional; ten-seed grok-rates have substantial uncertainty. Grokking is summarized by best held-out accuracy at τ = 0.70, which collapses trajectory information. The mechanistic output-periodicity measure is acknowledged to be partly definitional, and the embedding result does not establish the full causal circuit. Scale generalization is explicitly open.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted from the retained reported conditions; figure-only graphical values without explicit numerical descriptions were not transcribed. Cited results from other studies were excluded.

untested.parts: How the delay scales with training-set size: only one trajectory is shown, and the coverage sweeps report best-accuracy grok-rates.
All: there is no time-resolved circuit formation or cleanup, and no progress measure anticipating the jump.
All: there is no non-algorithmic data and no manipulation of initialization scale or weight norm.
The circuit-efficiency mechanism itself, and ungrokking below the critical size.
All: the read-out is agnostic to which algorithm a seed implements.
All: there is no control of adaptive-optimizer instability or softmax floating-point collapse, and no delay measure. The reduction-order and device perturbations are recorded under fits_no_version.

missing.what: Direct (a·b+c·d) mod 10 at ~8% coverage, weight decay 0.01: 0/10 grok. The monolith needs ~800–2,000 composite examples to grok (2–4/10).

record.verdict_notes: The model is pretrained (on 500K tokens) before fine-tuning, which may itself act as an inductive bias. The reader's V7 'challenges' label was dropped. V7 concerns optimizer and softmax artifacts producing the delay; this study neither controls those nor measures delay. Its null result is on reduction order and device, so those rows went to fits_no_version. The coverage rows were relinked from V1 to V5, since grok-rate cannot show delay. Coverage tables use only 3–5 seeds per cell.

versions.untested_parts: The study shows a held-out-accuracy trajectory for one task and coverage sweeps, but does not measure how the delay changes with training-set size or establish a long interval after training accuracy saturates across the coverage conditions.
No time-resolved circuit-formation or memorizing-component-removal measure, and no continuous progress measure shown to anticipate the generalization jump.
No non-algorithmic task comparison or initialization-scale/weight-norm manipulation testing a lazy-to-rich transition.
No realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning experiment.
Tests weight-decay effects and coverage-dependent grok-rates, but does not establish that low norm favors a more efficient circuit over memorization or test the account’s circuit-level mechanism.
No identification or comparison of the algorithms learned across runs; the mechanistic read-out is deliberately agnostic to which algorithm a seed implements.
Tests CPU thread count and CPU-versus-GPU numerical-environment changes, but not adaptive-optimizer instabilities or softmax-collapse control.

rows.stage_stated: pretrained on 500K tokens of FineWeb-Edu; fine-tuned
rows.operation_detail: Measured training and held-out accuracy and cross-entropy over training for (a+b) mod 10.
rows.measure: Training and held-out accuracy and answer-token cross-entropy over epochs; held-out transition epochs ≈320–760; training accuracy leads held-out by at most a few tenths.
rows.baseline: Chance accuracy 1/M; chance loss ln M ≈ 2.30.
rows.value: All ten seeds grok; held-out accuracy stays near chance before transitioning sharply, while training and held-out loss plateau at chance before collapsing.
rows.uncertainty: not stated
rows.locator: Figure 1; Section 3, “What the best-accuracy summary collapses”
rows.note: The authors say the train–held-out gap is brief and memorization precedes generalization only narrowly at this scale, rather than for a long interval.
rows.check: The chance-to-near-perfect jump is observed, with transitions at epochs ~320–760. But the authors say training accuracy leads only briefly, so the long post-saturation delay V1 names is essentially absent here.

relationships.condition: Pretrained ~12K-parameter transformer; (a+b) mod 10 at 80% coverage, weight decay 0.1, ten seeds
relationships.reason: Held-out accuracy jumps sharply from chance at epochs ~320–760. But the authors say training leads only briefly, so there is no long memorization interval (r1).
relationships.display_finding: Held-out accuracy jumped sharply from chance around epochs 320–760, but training led only briefly.

source_check.condition: Pretrained ~12K-parameter transformer; (a+b) mod 10 at 80% coverage, weight decay 0.1, ten seeds
source_check.reason: Figure 1 and Section 3 support r1: held-out accuracy changes sharply at approximately epochs 320–760, but the training lead is brief rather than a long interval after memorization.

relationships.condition: Composite mod-M tasks across coverage and training budgets; (a+b) mod 10 at weight decay 0.1 vs 0
relationships.reason: There is a sharp, near all-or-nothing coverage threshold (0/3–0/5 below, 3/3–5/5 above; r2–r14), consistent with a critical dataset size. Grok-rate rises with n in mid-transition cells (r16→r20, r18→r22). Weight decay of 0.1 lifts grok-rate from 20% to 90% (r30 vs r28).
relationships.display_finding: Grokking shifted sharply from 0/3–0/5 runs below the coverage threshold to 3/3–5/5 above it, with larger n improving success near the transition, while weight decay of 0.1 increased grokking frequency from 20% to 90% on addition modulo 10.

source_check.condition: Composite mod-M tasks across coverage and training budgets; (a+b) mod 10 at weight decay 0.1 vs 0
source_check.reason: Tables 1–2 support the coverage-threshold results cited as r2–r22; Table 3 supports the 20% to 90% increase cited as r28 and r30. These support the critical-data-size and beneficial-decay components; circuit efficiency and ungrokking remain untested.

relationships.condition: (a+b) mod 10 at 80% coverage with weight decay 0, 0.01 and 1.0
relationships.reason: 20% of seeds grok with no weight decay (r28). Decay of 0.01 gives no reliable gain (27%, r29). Decay of 1.0 collapses learning to 0% (r31), so the low-norm benefit holds only in a window.
relationships.display_finding: Grokking occurred in 20% of seeds without decay and 27% with decay 0.01, while decay 1.0 collapsed learning to 0%.

labels.reason: Figure 1 and Section 3 support r1: held-out accuracy changes sharply at approximately epochs 320–760, but the training lead is brief rather than a long interval after memorization.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: Composite mod-M tasks across coverage and training budgets; (a+b) mod 10 at weight decay 0.1 vs 0
labels.reason: Tables 1–2 support the coverage-threshold results cited as r2–r22; Table 3 supports the 20% to 90% increase cited as r28 and r30. These support the critical-data-size and beneficial-decay components; circuit efficiency and ungrokking remain untested.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: (a+b) mod 10 at 80% coverage with weight decay 0, 0.01 and 1.0
labels.reason: Table 3 supports r28, r29 and r31: reported grok-rates are 20%, 27% and 0%. The benefit of decay is conditional on its strength; excessive decay destroys learning. Grokking without decay alone does not refute V5.

relation.reason: The study reports its own accuracy trajectories and interventions on training coverage and weight decay.

tranche.reason: Fine-tuning a pretrained toy transformer and measuring multi-seed grok-rates tests grokking with a different experimental method from the original.

source_check.notes: Source inconsistencies: Table 3 reports 27% despite stating ten seeds per condition; Figure 1 reports 10/10 at decay 0.1 while Table 3 reports 90% for the apparently same setting. The checked records reproduce these source claims.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: (a+b) mod 10 at 80% coverage and weight decay 0.1; other coverage conditions summarized by best held-out grok-rate
reader_labels.reason: The trajectory shows a chance-level held-out plateau followed by a sharp transition, but the authors say training leads held-out by at most a few tenths and the memorization gap is brief; the coverage tables do not measure delay. Rows r1–r27 and r40–r45.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: (a+b) mod 10 at 80% coverage; composite-task coverage sweeps and budgets
reader_labels.reason: Grok-rate rises from 20% to 90% and then falls to 0% across the weight-decay sweep; the coverage results also show sharp task-dependent grok-rate transitions, though they do not test the circuit-efficiency mechanism. Rows r2–r31.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: CPU thread-count and CPU-versus-GPU comparisons, at τ = 0.70
reader_labels.reason: The paired numerical changes flip some individual seed outcomes but produce no detectable aggregate grok-rate shift, contrary to a numerical-choice account in which the measured aggregate grokking disappears when controlled. Rows r32 and r34.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Individual seed outcomes and alternative thresholds
reader_labels.reason: Numerical settings do alter outcomes for a minority of paired seeds, and the device flip count varies with threshold; these results qualify the aggregate null without testing optimizer instability or softmax collapse. Rows r32–r35.
